notes.title: Restrung Patch Notes May 22
notes.content:
- Reduced file size thanks to improved audio compression

- Removed a cutscene trigger after its corresponding cutscene has finished playing

- Adjusted the volume of a song during a cutscene

- Fixed some text formatting

- Fixed improper scaling of collision box for an object late in the game

- Fixed issue in which custom gamepad inputs would not load

- Fixed issue in which incorrect dialogue would be displayed during the game's intro depending on the player's input during their first playthrough

notes.title: Update 1.2.5
notes.content:
Patch notes:

- Added option to unequip equipable items
- [i][b]Permanently[/b][/i] fixed issue where the user was, under some conditions, able to select "Continue" despite not having a save file, resulting in a softlock on the title screen
- Attempting to interact with the crystal switches used in a handful of puzzles several times consecutively in a short time frame would crash the game. This has been fixed.
- Players were forced to rewatch a late-game cutscene (and walk through the area leading up to it) if they failed to defeat the boss that followed said cutscene. This has been changed, and players are now able to face the boss without having to replay the part leading up to it.
- Interacting with a tree found in the game's first area at a specific point in progression would crash the game. This has been fixed.
- In two particular character interactions, your previous inputs would, under some conditions, influence the dialogue of the character you were talking to, leading to dialogue from different "branches" being mixed up. This has been fixed, and one new line of dialogue has been added for one of the dialogue choices to make the end of the conversation feel less abrupt.

DEVELOPER NOTE:
I received an email about a game crash that would occur after obtaining Tay's old guitar from the mayor, then going to the diner and asking for a glass of milk. (Thanks again for the report, by the way!) 
However, after having played through the opening and performing a variety of different actions prior to the point where the game is "supposed" to crash, I was unable to replicate it on both the Steam and Itch builds of the game. If anyone else is able to replicate this from a fresh save file, I would love to hear how you were able to get it to happen. Until I'm able to find the exact cause of it, I won't be able to fix it. Even looking through the code, I'm unable to see how the error that was spat out was even produced. It could be a machine-specific thing. I've tried this on both my PC and laptop, and my playtesters have run into no issues regarding the interaction.
(For anyone who's encountered any major bugs, feel free to get in touch via bootcatstudio@gmail.com !)

notes.title: Customisable input-mappings and additional accessibility features coming soon!
notes.content:
Hi, everyone! DISHARMONY has now been out for about 3½ days, and I thought it would be nice to give people an idea of what kind of updates to expect in the near future.

As you will be aware if you've played the game for pretty much any time at all, the game does not currently allow you to change its default input-mapping, that is to say, you [i]have to[/i] use the default controls. While most players so far seem to be fine with the default controls, I definitely understand why some people may find the lack of customisability frustrating.
This is going to change in the near future. I plan on implementing another screen for the options menu where you're able to change the rhythm inputs to pretty much anything you want. The only difficult part is ensuring the inputs don't cause contradictions (It would be pretty strange if you could map one key to press every button, or something of the sort).
I can't say for sure when this update will be released, but I'll make sure to release another announcement here once it's ready.

I'm also planning on expanding the amount of accessibility features for the game. 
Currently, the game offers one accessibility option, which adds an equipable difficulty-reducing item to your inventory. While this does make the game much easier, and ensures pretty much everyone can get through the game, I do want there to be more options for those who still wish to experience the game more-or-less as intended.
The first additional features to be added while likely be:

- The ability to disable note-spam punishment damage
- The ability to hold down a key to hit a note, instead of pressing it

The ability to disable boss/enemy gimmicks will also be added in the future, but this requires significantly more work, and will therefor take longer to implement and release.
(If you have suggestions for other potential features that might help more people play the game, please get in touch!)

That will be all for now.

Thank you for playing DISHARMONY!
